title: Audit the affine-orbit averaging and pinned-majority threshold results
objective: Independently audit the recent affine-orbit / stabilizer-overlap claims, with particular attention to the promised input classes, uniformity, polynomial dependence on binary input size and 1/epsilon, and the exact boundary between tractable affine cases and the stated width-three hardness result.
scope: Check the stated invariant-flag and block-semi-linear hypotheses and how they are represented in the input.
Audit the construction of the small permutation quotient, kernel generators, diagonal conjugates, and unitriangular normal closure.
Verify the polynomial-size averaging list and the spectral-gap / derandomized-squaring argument.
Audit all polynomial bounds, including residue-ring arithmetic for composite q-1, matrix word lengths, and dependence on 1/epsilon.
Separate the exact-majority tractable result from the strict-majority width-three hardness claim; verify that the thresholds and promise models are not conflated.
deliverables: An explicit theorem statement with the exact input representation and promises.
Proof audit of each group-theoretic construction and complexity bound.
Independent implementation or small exhaustive checks for the finite algebraic steps, clearly labeled as finite evidence.
Identification of any missing uniformity, hidden exponential factor, or unsupported subroutine.
A precise statement of what this restricted result says and does not say about SAT or P vs NP.
acceptance_criteria: All algorithms must run in time polynomial in the encoded input size and 1/epsilon under the stated hypotheses.
Distinguish abstract existence of a generating set from an efficiently constructible list.
Check ring operations over composite moduli rather than assuming field Gaussian elimination.
Do not extrapolate the restricted affine group result to unrestricted SAT or general affine generators.
Report counterexamples and exact proof gaps rather than smoothing over them.
